title: On Venus, a Rotation Takes Longer Than a Year
post_title: On Venus, a Rotation Takes Longer Than a Year | QuantaTale
post_description: Imagine a planet where one rotation takes longer than its trip around the Sun. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/ https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Venus_Express/Venus_compared_to_Earth #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Venus has a calendar that sounds impossible. One rotation of Venus relative to the distant stars takes longer than one orbit around the Sun. So its day, measured against the stars, is longer than its year. Venus also rotates in the opposite direction to most planets, meaning the Sun would rise in the west. Be careful with the word day: a Venus solar day, from one noon to the next, is shorter than that star-measured day.
